The symbols of Block Diffusion RooflinesPrevious: 8 · Conclusion

This page lists every symbol of the blogpost, with its meaning and the place where it is introduced. The values in parentheses are those of DiffusionGemma 26B-A4B and of an H200. In the other chapters, a click on a formula lists the symbols that it uses.

Decoding

SymbolMeaningIntroduced
\(\Gamma\)throughput gain: tokens per second of TD over those of ARProposition 1
\(B\)batch: sequences decoded togetherPart 1
\(C\)context: tokens already in the KV cache of each sequencePart 1
\(b\)canvas length, in tokens (256)Part 1
\(S\)denoising passes per canvas (14)Part 1
\(r\)cost of a denoising pass relative to a commit pass, i.e., a forward pass of the causal encoder (1)Part 1
\(\omega = Sr + 1\)forward passes that one canvas costs (15)Part 1
\(\mathrm{TPF} = b/\omega\)tokens committed per forward pass (17.07)Part 1
\(P,\ G\)prompt tokens and generated tokens per sequence (1,024 and 8,192)Part 3
\(\lambda\)logit-sized reads and writes of HBM per output position (5 for TD, 2 for AR); 0 means the logits stay on-chipPart 3
\(t\)noise level of a canvas, from 1 to 0 over the denoising passes (Figure 2); in Parts 5–8, \(t\) is a measured timePart 0
\(\Delta t\)step of the noise level from one denoising pass to the next, \(1/S\)Part 0
\(x_0\)clean canvas, the target of the denoising passes (Figure 2)Part 0
\(s_t\)self-conditioning signal: the previous pass's prediction, fed back to the next pass (Figure 2)Part 0

Accelerator and precision

SymbolMeaningIntroduced
\(\pi\)peak FLOPs per second of the accelerator, on matrix multiplications (989 TFLOP/s on an H200)Part 1
\(\beta\)memory bandwidth of the accelerator, in bytes per second (4.8 TB/s on an H200)Part 1
\(I^\star = \pi/\beta\)ridge point of the accelerator: a pass is compute-bound when its intensity reaches it (206 on an H200)Definition 3
\(s_w\)bytes per weight (2 in BF16, 16-bit floats; 1 in FP8, 8-bit floats)Definition 1
\(s_{\mathrm{kv}}\)bytes per element of the KV cache (2)Definition 1
\(\kappa^c\)K/V tensors that a layer caches per KV head and per token (2: keys and values stored separately; 1 for a global layer whose \(K = V\) is stored once)Definition 1

Model

SymbolMeaningIntroduced
\(L\)layers (30)Definition 1
\(d\)hidden size (2816)Part 2
\(V\)vocabulary size (262,144)Part 3
\(\mathcal G,\ \mathcal W,\ \mathcal S\)sets of the global-attention, sliding-window and sparse layers (5, 25 and none in DiffusionGemma)Definition 1
\(w\)window of a sliding-window layer, which sees at most \(w\) earlier tokens (1,023)Definition 1
\(n_q,\ n_{\mathrm{kv},\ell}\)query heads and KV heads of a layer (16 query heads; 2 KV heads on the global layers, 8 on the window layers)Definition 1
\(h_\ell\)head dimension of layer \(\ell\) (512 on the global layers, 256 on the window layers)Definition 1
\(g\)query heads per KV head on the global layers, \(n_q/n_{\mathrm{kv},\ell}\) (8)Definition 1
\(E\)experts per MoE layer (128)Definition 1
\(k\)experts each token selects (8)Definition 1
\(W^e\)parameters of one expert in one layer, \(3d\,f_E\) (5.95M)Definition 1
\(f_E\)width of one expert (704)Part 3
\(W_{\mathrm{ne}}\)non-expert parameters of all layers (1.66B for DiffusionGemma)Definition 1
\(N_{\mathrm{act}}\)parameters active per token, \(W_{\mathrm{ne}} + LkW^e\) (3.08B for DiffusionGemma, without the vocabulary)Definition 2
\(W_{\mathrm{tot}}\)all parameters, \(W_{\mathrm{ne}} + LEW^e\) (24.5B, without the vocabulary)Proposition 4
\(m\)cached tokens each query selects in a sparse layer (2048 in the sparse variant)Definition 1
\(n_{I,\ell}\)heads of the indexer of sparse layer \(\ell\), \(n_I\) when the layer is clear (8)Definition 1
\(h_{I,\ell},\ s_I\)head dimension of the indexer of sparse layer \(\ell\) (\(h_I\) when the layer is clear) and bytes per element of its keys (128, 1 in FP8)Definition 1
\(\mathcal M_i\)tokens that query \(i\) selects in a sparse layerRemark 1
\(z_{i,j},\ \gamma_{i,a}\)the indexer's score of cached token \(j\) for query \(i\), and the query-dependent weight of indexer head \(a\)Remark 1
\(q^I_{i,a},\ k^I_j\)the indexer's query of head \(a\) for query \(i\), and its key of cached token \(j\), shared by its headsRemark 1

Costs and intensities

SymbolMeaningIntroduced
\(F,\ Q\)FLOPs and bytes of one pass, per sequenceDefinition 2
\(\nu\)KV-cache bytes per cached token (G: global, W: windowed, S: sparse layers, I: indexer)Definition 1
\(\alpha\)attention FLOPs per query and per cached token (same subscripts as \(\nu\))Definition 1
\(\class{mj-ar}{W^{\mathrm{AR}}}\)weights an AR step reads at batch \(B\), in parametersDefinition 2
\(\class{mj-td}{W^{\mathrm{TD}}}\)weights a TD pass reads at batch \(B\), in parametersDefinition 2
\(U_{E,k}(N)\)expected number of distinct experts that \(N\) positions touch in a layer (\(E = 128\) experts, \(k = 8\) per token)Definition 2
\(U_{C,m}(N)\)cached tokens that \(N\) queries read together in a sparse layer, each selecting \(m\): the coverage function \(U_{n,k}\) of Definition 1 with \(n = C\) and \(k = m\), so \(U_{C,m}(1) = \min(C, m)\)Definition 2
\(\class{mj-ar}{I^{\mathrm{AR}}}\)arithmetic intensity of one AR step: its FLOPs per byte read from HBMDefinition 3
\(\class{mj-td}{I^{\mathrm{TD}}}\)arithmetic intensity of one TD pass over a canvas of \(b\) positions: its FLOPs per byte read from HBMDefinition 3
\(I^X_{\mathrm{lin}}\)linear part of an intensity: linear-layer FLOPs over weight bytesDefinition 3
\(I^X_{\mathrm{attn}}\)attention part of an intensity: attention FLOPs over KV-cache bytesDefinition 3
\(I_{\mathrm{lin}}\)linear part of an AR step's intensity, \(\class{mj-ar}{I^{\mathrm{AR}}_{\mathrm{lin}}}\) (1.0 at batch 1, 8.2 at batch 64; the batch \(B\) for a dense model in BF16)Definition 3
\(I_{\mathrm{attn}}\)attention FLOPs per cache byte for one query on a global layer (8 for DiffusionGemma)Definition 3
\(I_{\mathrm{win}}\)attention FLOPs per cache byte for one query on a window layer (2 for DiffusionGemma)Definition 3
\(I_{\mathrm{idx}}\)FLOPs per cache byte of a sparse layer's index scan for one queryDefinition 3
\(\theta\)share of the bytes of a pass carried by one of its partsProposition 2
\(\theta_E\)expert share of the weights that an AR step readsProposition 3
\(\sigma\)window layers' FLOPs per query over the linear FLOPs, \(\alpha_W w/(2N_{\mathrm{act}})\) (6.8%)Proposition 7
\(C_F\)context at which global attention alone matches the linear FLOPs (37.6k)Proposition 7
\(F_c,\ Q_c\)FLOPs and bytes of one kernel class (component) \(c\) of a passPart 1
\(\class{mj-ar}{T^{\mathrm{AR}}},\ \class{mj-td}{T^{\mathrm{TD}}}\)time per generated token of AR and of TD, in the proof of Proposition 1Proposition 1
\(N\)positions that share a selected resource in one pass (\(B\) or \(Bb\) for the experts, 1 or \(b\) for the cached tokens of a sparse layer)Definition 4
\(x\)share of an AR step's bytes spent on one part (weights in Proposition 5, cache in Proposition 7); elsewhere a hidden state (Remark 1) or a layer input (Part 7)Proposition 5
\(I_n\)intensity of a pass that routes \(n\) positions per sequence (\(I_1 = \class{mj-ar}{I^{\mathrm{AR}}}\), \(I_b = \class{mj-td}{I^{\mathrm{TD}}}\))Proposition 8
\(W_n\)weights that such a pass reads (\(W_1 = \class{mj-ar}{W^{\mathrm{AR}}}\), \(W_b = \class{mj-td}{W^{\mathrm{TD}}}\))Proposition 8

Penalties

SymbolMeaningIntroduced
\(\Pi\)overall penalty: bytes per sequence of a TD pass over those of an AR stepDefinition 4
\(\Pi_{\mathrm{lin}}\)linear penalty: weight bytes a TD pass reads over those an AR step reads (7.9 at batch 1, 1 at large batch)Definition 4
\(\Pi_{\mathrm{attn}}\)attention penalty: cache bytes a TD pass reads over those an AR step reads (1 for dense and windowed attention)Definition 4
\(\Pi_E\)distinct experts a TD pass touches over those an AR step touchesDefinition 4
\(\Pi_{\mathrm{sel}}\)selection penalty: cached tokens a canvas selects in a sparse layer over those one query selectsDefinition 4
\(\zeta\)independent fraction of a canvas's selections: 1 when independent, \(1/b\) when every query selects the same tokensPart 2

Thresholds and regimes

SymbolMeaningIntroduced
\(\class{mj-td}{B^{\mathrm{TD}}_\star}\)batch at which a TD pass reaches the ridge, \(\class{mj-td}{I^{\mathrm{TD}}} = I^\star\); the best batch when AR is memory-boundCorollary 1
\(\class{mj-ar}{B^{\mathrm{AR}}_\star}\)smallest batch at which an AR step is compute-boundCorollary 2
\(B_\times\)parity batch: beyond it AR is fasterCorollary 2
\(b_c\)critical canvas length \(I^\star/I_{\mathrm{attn}}\): above it a longer context helps TD reach the ridgeProposition 8
A1–A3the assumptions of Proposition 1Part 1
\(C_{\mathrm{lin}}(B, x)\)context below which the weights are at least a share \(x\) of an AR step's bytesProposition 5
\(B^\star_n(C),\ D_n(C)\)smallest compute-bound batch for \(n\) queries per sequence at context \(C\), and the FLOPs per sequence left for the weightsProposition 8

Measurements

SymbolMeaningIntroduced
\(\hat\pi\)empirical compute ceiling: the highest FLOP rate measured on this H200 (for attention, FlashAttention 3's sustained rate) (FP8 1,468, BF16 781, attention 638 TFLOP/s)Definition 5
\(\hat\beta\)empirical bandwidth: 4.32 TB/s measured on this H200Definition 5
\(\tau_c\)empirical roofline time of a component \(c\): \(\max(F_c/\hat\pi_c,\ Q_c/\hat\beta)\)Definition 5
\(\tau^X\)empirical roofline time of a step of decoder \(X\) (\(\class{mj-ar}{\tau^{\mathrm{AR}}}\), \(\class{mj-td}{\tau^{\mathrm{TD}}}\)): the sum \(\sum_c \tau_c\) over its componentsDefinition 5
\(t^X,\ t_c\)measured time of a step (\(\class{mj-ar}{t^{\mathrm{AR}}}\), \(\class{mj-td}{t^{\mathrm{TD}}}\)) or of a component (\(t_c\))Definition 7
\(\eta^X,\ \eta_c\)efficiency: roofline time over measured time (1 means at the roofline)Definition 7
\(n^X\)tokens a step commits: \(B\) for AR, \(Bb/\omega\) for TDProposition 9
\(\Gamma_{\mathrm{meas}}\)measured gain: TD tokens per second over AR tokens per secondProposition 9
\(\Gamma_{\mathrm{roof}}\)roofline bound at the measured ceilings and routingProposition 9
\(U_{\mathrm{meas}}\)distinct experts per layer that a pass touches, measuredDefinition 6
\(U_{\mathrm{freq}}\)distinct experts predicted from the measured expert frequencies, tokens independentDefinition 6
\(N_{\mathrm{eff}}\)effective independent tokens: the \(N\) at which \(U_{E,k}(N)\) equals the measured countDefinition 6
\(\rho_e\)frequency with which a token selects expert \(e\)Definition 6
\(\mu\)rows per touched expert, \(Nk/U\)Part 7
\(M_q,\ M_k\)query rows and keys of one attention tilePart 7
\(\mathbf{Q},\ \mathbf{K},\ \mathbf{V}\)query, key and value tiles of one attention block, split in two halves \(\mathbf{Q}_0, \mathbf{Q}_1\) (bold: not the bytes \(Q\))Part 7
\(\mathbf{O}_i\)output rows of query tile \(i\)Part 7
\(U\)experts touched by \(N\) tokens in one MoE layer (\(U_{\mathrm{meas}}\) when measured)Part 7
\(\mathbf{Z}\)attention scores \(\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^\top\) of one tilePart 7
\(h\)head dimension of a global layer (512)Part 7
\(\eta^\star_c\)target efficiency of a component: that of the best kernel timed alone at representative shapes (the mean of three for global attention), 0.8 where none was timedDefinition 7
\(\Delta t_c\)recoverable time of a component, \(\max(0,\ t_c - \tau_c/\eta^\star_c)\)Definition 7
\(p_{i,e}\)routing weight of expert \(e\) for token \(i\)Part 7
\(\delta\)scale shared by a block of FP8 values, which stores \(x\) as \(\mathrm{round}(x/\delta)\)Part 7
\(a_{i,e}\)activation of token \(i\) in expert \(e\)Part 7
\(W_g,\ W_u\)gate and up matrices of an expertPart 7
\(W_d\)down matrix of an expertPart 7
